source.title: Empirical Materials for The Persistence of the Harvest in Medieval England
source.creator: Cliff T. Bekar

semantics.direct_model_unit_conversion: requires the dataset's documented yield-unit definition and crop-specific mass conversion; no seed-rate imputation is allowed
semantics.model_target_relation: realized historical demesne yield, not intrinsic 1337 attainable potential

why_this_is_relevant: Unlike the BAHS public workbook used in the current pipeline, the replication file explicitly contains yields per acre rather than yield per seed.
The study covers 1211-1349, overlapping the game-start technology window and the existing England anchor.

The metadata exposes soil, husbandry, farm strategy, precipitation and temperature fields that can be used for a source-family holdout or a realized-to-attainable gap diagnostic rather than a location population target.

current_status.reason: The file is independently identified but not yet downloaded, checksum-pinned, parsed, and crosswalked. It cannot close the attainable-yield gate by metadata alone.

required_ingestion_steps: Obtain the file under the repository's source-download policy and record its SHA-256.
Parse the Stata period columns without imputing missing values; preserve crop, period, manor and source identifiers.
Resolve the study's yield-per-acre unit definition and convert to kg dry matter per hectare using cited crop mass/acre conversions only.
Map the 38 manors to EU5 locations or quantified province footprints; report unmapped and mixed-boundary observations.
Compare GAEZ/PyAEZ attainable labels to realized yields as an explicitly one-sided attainable-to-realized diagnostic, not as a direct population target.
Add independent crop-risk and parameter uncertainty scenarios before promoting any uncertainty flag.
